chunks: And Ali ibn al-Husayn informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hassan al-Razi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Mahboob al-Zarrad, from Abu al-Mughra, from Abdullah ibn Abu Ya'foor, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he heard him saying:

Woe to the arrogant ones of the Arabs from an evil that has drawn near. I said: May I be your ransom, how many of the Arabs will be with the Qa'im (peace be upon him)? He said: A small number. I said: By Allah, those who describe this matter among them are many. He said: People must be purified, distinguished, and sifted, and a great multitude will be thrown out from the sieve.

key_terms.طُغَاةُ الْعَرَبِ: The arrogant/haughty ones of the Arabs

ai.seo_question: How many Arabs will follow the Qa'im according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In the context of the Minor and Major Ghaiba, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the true core of the Qa'im's army will be small, serving as a divine sieve (gharbala) to purify the Shia from pretenders and those with hidden defects. This narration underscores the Shia scholarly view that numerical majority does not equate to spiritual correctness, emphasizing the necessity of distinguishing sincere adherents from the 'wicked' during the period of concealment. The metaphor of sifting highlights the eschatological function of trials in refining the community's identity before the final victory.
